sp.p: That's a funny question to put to a man in his own room! Miss Ruth–Mary, or whatever your name may be–for the first time I've learned, just now, that eighteen years ago this staunch, plucky fellow – (slapping Joe on the shoulders)

sp.speaker: Joe.
sp.l: I say, my lad, draw it mild!–I blushes easy.

sp.speaker: Kit.
sp.p: Saved you from a fire! These things belong to you. (to Joe) So you say.

sp.speaker: Joe.
sp.p: And so I'll swear! I kept them as proof of her iden-ti-ti-ittity–confound the word! That's her little coral necklace, and them's her little socks

sp.speaker: Kit.
sp.p: Marked "M. D." On this little toy of my childhood (going to kit on the wall) are rudely traced the words "J. D., his fiddle."

sp.speaker: Mike.
sp.l: What the deuce is coming now ?

sp.speaker: Philip.
sp.l: Well, sir, what then?

sp.speaker: Kit.
sp.p: Wait a bit. My earliest recollections of just eighteen years ago are of a fire, too. The night before it happened–it has often come before me like a dream–I remember a struggle with a little child, almost an infant then for the possession of a picture book she had clutched in her little hands: one half of such a picture book I found among the treasured relics in Joe's drawer, the other half I have preserved through all these years. See, here it is! (takes it out of drawer) See, see ! they match! (crossing to Honor) That child then, was Ruth. Didn't I always say, Honor, it would bring me good luck? Ruth, have you no memory of the past, to help me?

sp.speaker: Joe.
sp.p: Bless the boy, how should she? She could only lisp one word.

sp.speaker: Kit.
sp.p: One word. Yes, yes, it comes back to me now. The child I fondled–yes, it lisped to me, "Donny," " Donny."

sp.speaker: Joe.
sp.p: That's it! he's got it all right, "Donny." I'll be blessed if you won't turn out to be "Donny" yourself! (to Honor) Hang me, if she didn't mean Johnny–lor' how came we never to think of that!

sp.speaker: Philip.
sp.l: But can you suppose I shall allow myself to be duped by this concerted plot?

sp.speaker: Joe.
sp.p: Concerted plot! That's very kind of you, very flattering. But our heads are not clear enough for that line of business. We leaves plots and swindles for the likes of you, and him there, to think of.

sp.speaker: Philip.
sp.p: But the law will require clearer proofs (crosses to door, L. C.) but whatever the law may decide, I shall only be too happy to rid myself of a pack of low creatures, who call themselves my relations.

div.stage: Exit, door L. C.

sp.speaker: Joe.
sp.p: Don't you be too sure that they would be proud of the relationship. Take care of them curly whiskers, as you go down stairs.

sp.speaker: Mike.
sp.p: Though I'm a 'cute player at most games, I own I've lost the trick. But I don't bear malice.

sp.speaker: Joe.
sp.l: Don't you? – now that's really affecting!

sp.speaker: Mike.
sp.l: I salute the fair sex.

sp.speaker: Honor.
sp.l: The least dirty way of doing it is by showing a clean pair of heels.

sp.speaker: Mike.
sp.l: I only wish I had you out at the diggings, my gal!

div.stage: Exit angrily, door L. C.

sp.speaker: Joe.
sp.l: I say, leave us a lock of your hair.

sp.speaker: Kit.
sp.stage: (who has been putting Mike's things into a bundle, now flings it after him)
sp.p: And you'd better take all your valuable property with you, for you won't have a chance of coming here to fetch it, I can tell you.

sp.speaker: Joe.
sp.p: How I wish I'd had hose and pumps in good working order. I'd have helped those chaps down stairs, rather. St. Swithin would have been a joke compared to me.

sp.speaker: Kit.
sp.p: And now, Miss Honor, with Joe's permission, I'll claim your promise. (Joe looks surprised–Ruth explains matters to him)

sp.speaker: Honor.
sp.l: Promise! What have you done? Nothing at all.

sp.speaker: Kit.
sp.p: Little enough, I know. But I have found you here in my room, and you know what you once said. So now I claim the forfeit.

sp.speaker: Honor.
sp.l: Oh! the monster! I never came, 'twas Joe, and–

sp.speaker: Kit.
sp.p: Well then (putting his hands before his eyes) I don't see you. I only dreamed it with my eyes open, take back your word.

sp.speaker: Honor.
sp.p: I do, but to give it back again for life, and of my own free will.

sp.speaker: Joe.
sp.p: Come that's jolly! Shan't we make a lively family party for a dance? Giving hands across and back again, no not back again. What a proud chap I do feel to be sure. The public have given me medals and testimonials, and all sorts of praise for one deed or another. And I'm sure you, Ruth, and you Honor, and you master Kit, as well as many friends around me, know that it is only to say the word to Joe Bright, and to serve one and all he is always ready to go "Through Fire And Water."

div.stage: Curtain.
